alignments.note: Expletive There, the copula, and the adverb there are all helpers on the lexical verb; head on set per rule 17.
Anarthrous Greek, so the supplied indefinite is an ordinary helper on the noun (rule 51).
No article here, so the case preposition stays with the noun and heads on it (rules 17, 21).
Participle rendered finite; the supplied subject pronoun is its helper (rules 7, 9).
Article carries the case preposition; of the is one unit headed on the (rule 21).
Anarthrous dative; upon realizes the case and rides with the noun rather than the compound verb (rules 21, 36).

The coordinating and is an obligatory juncture helper on the verb it introduces, and the supplied object it has no Greek token of its own; giving it to the verb rather than reading it off the genitive pronoun is the defensible analysis, though an added it remains arguable.
Displaced by the possessive his, which belongs to the genitive pronoun (rule 20).
Discontinuous: the case preposition stays with the noun since the article is displaced (rules 15, 20, 21).
